name: Citizenship by Descent

qualifying_event.description: A child of a Jordanian father is Jordanian wherever born (Nationality Law No. 6 of 1954, Article 9). A child born in Jordan to a Jordanian mother acquires Jordanian nationality only where the father's nationality is unknown or he is stateless (Article 4) -- a Jordanian mother married to a known foreign-national father cannot pass citizenship to her child through descent.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificate; proof of father's Jordanian nationality (or, for the narrow maternal exception, proof the father is unknown or stateless).

requirements.blocker_text: The father is a Jordanian citizen; the child is Jordanian wherever born (Article 9).

requirement_groups.name: Child of a Jordanian mother, father unknown or stateless

requirements.blocker_text: Born in Jordan to a Jordanian mother, where the father's nationality is unknown or he is stateless (Article 4).

evidence_required.document: Proof of father's Jordanian nationality (paternal route) or proof father is unknown/stateless (maternal exception)

sources.title: Refworld (UNHCR) -- Jordan Nationality Law No. 6 of 1954, as amended to 1987: Article 9 (patrilineal citizenship by descent, unconditional), Article 4 (narrow maternal exception where the father is unknown or stateless)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Jordan). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-2 sourced (see jo_citizenship_naturalisation.json for the same sourcing caveat). Jordan's descent framework is strictly patrilineal by default: a Jordanian mother married to a known foreign father CANNOT pass citizenship to her children under this law -- a genuinely disclosed structural absence, not modeled as a general maternal route. This has been a long-documented point of domestic and international criticism of Jordanian nationality law and directly produces statelessness/residency complications for the children of Jordanian women married to foreign men, distinct from and compounding the jo_citizenship_by_marriage.json asymmetry (a Jordanian woman's foreign husband also has no citizenship-by-marriage route). Children in this situation are typically eligible only for renewable residency and work-permit exemptions administratively, not citizenship -- these administrative accommodations were referenced in secondary sources during research but not confirmed in enough procedural detail to model as their own route in this pass.
